Sequential assessment 2026-09-12: confirmed current reproducibility defect in repository browser/demo pages, retained P3 under core-first scope. surface-view-three/browser/index.html and surface-view/browser/{index,morph,cortical,lens,threshold-parity}.html still import from a sibling jscode/surfviewjs/node_modules path; no package/lock file was found in these example/backend directories. This is not evidence of a core renderer algorithm defect or a request to update every Scala.js module kind.

Bounded acceptance refinement:
- Declare and lock a Three.js dependency at a documented repository/browser-tooling root; pick its version from fresh compatibility evidence, not the historical Neuropublish version assertion alone. Make every affected page resolve it without sibling checkouts.
- Document dependency installation, Scala.js linking and an HTTP serving root, so a clean checkout has a complete reproducible path (npm install alone does not produce the Scala.js main.js).
- Current pages deliberately consume exports through window.exports while passing an imported THREE object. Preserve that working entrypoint contract or migrate only the relevant example/probe entrypoints with their host scripts. A global CommonJS-to-ESModule change is not a prerequisite.
- Verify each affected page and its actual pixel/pick/admission receipt from that clean setup; zero import/console errors alone is insufficient. Qualify the selected Three.js version rather than asserting compatibility from a successful install or link.
- Keep runtime provider/version policy and external Vite adoption separate; no external application changes or browser runs are claimed by this assessment.
